answer: Each agent must bond a scarce resource, such as a small deposit, before it can submit work, and the protocol releases that bond only after other agents validate its result. A hidden, randomly chosen sample of tasks is rechecked; a false claim can forfeit the bond and bar the identity from future rounds. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must lock up capital in every one and risks losing it on each caught lie. A jade market may ripple with honest demand, while yarrow-tagged tasks expose copied answers to review.
